name: Chessylite Blue
lede: Chessylite blue is an old name for azurite, the blue copper mineral, taken from the place in France where it was found.

sections.title: A mineral named for a mine
sections.body:
The Pigment Compendium lists chessylite as an alternative mineral name for azurite, a copper carbonate hydroxide [1]. It takes its name from Chessy in France, one of the places where the mineral occurs [1]. Church (1901) states that chessylite is the same as azurite and as blue verditer [1].

The screen swatch is a greyed teal blue, a cooler and duller color than the deep blue of good azurite, so it should be read as a chart color, not as a sample of the mineral. Nearby named colors include [[steel-blue]], [[cadet-blue]] and plain [[blue]], with [[azure]] as the word that shares the mineral's family.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This swatch appears in 117 of our 23,781 paintings, 0.49 per cent [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, at 14 of 1,674 paintings, 3.3 times the museums' baseline [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, which is the color tucked in the shadows and transitions [2]. All numbers are as photographed, and a color match is not a pigment test.

origin.named_after: Chessy, France, where the mineral occurs
